Thanks a lot of reporting!

Would it be possible for you to provide minimal project that exhibits this behavior?
@geoand I wish I had the time to do this, as I appreciate the work that the quarkus community does. But I am really overbooked with work at moment.

I completely understand. 
Just keep in mind however that a reproducer is the most surefire way for us to act on issues as quickly as possible and fix them before the next release.

> I completely understand.
> Just keep in mind however that a reproducer is the most surefire way for us to act on issues as quickly as possible and fix them before the next release.

Makes sense.  I will try to get some support on my end to make it easier for us to create bug reproducer projects, as I do see the value in providing this information.

Ok, got some help creating a reproducer. I wasn't able to reproduce the same error ( during the "build step" as in the exception above).  However, I got a similar exception with the same classes at runtime.

Here is the reproducer:  [repo](https://github.com/sean-scott-lr/quarkus-bug-reproducer)

It seems like the failure occurs in tests but not when the jar is used. 

@stuartwdouglas @wburns any idea what we can do to overcome this problem?

The exception I am seeing is:


My hunch is that the annotation processor being used by Infinispan is causing issues for the Quarkus tests.
One reason why I think this is a happening is because if I remove the dependency in Quarkus that brings in the Infinispan annotation processor (`org.infinispan.protostream:protostream-processor`) and simple replace it with with the `protostream` dependnecy, the application gets passed the exception (although it obviously doesn't work because there is no marshaller generated).

This is due to https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/commit/ae19472cc5c166d49a4a105597780de4366d89c0#diff-5c4067844056bb7ffd25622e4fa17116R36

Basically for safety we added in some additional checks for directory elements in the QuarkusClassLoader. Because of the way this project is laid out with parents and children next to each other the discovery generated paths with '../' in them, that interfere with the directory escape protection code.

issue.title: Make sure to use normalised paths

labels.name: area/devtools
labels.description: Issues/PR related to maven, gradle, platform and cli tooling/plugins

issue.body:
Non-heiracial maven project layouts may
result in paths with ../ path seperators,
which causes problems with directory escape
detection.

Fixes #9515
